assertion_audit.fails_if: Removing the `if fenced or placement.in_allocation` append at reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:778 leaves ["/usr/bin"] instead of the scheduler entry; leaving the inherited git shim in, or appending any other entry, fails the same exact-list comparison. A wrong shim_directory() value moves both sides and is not caught.

assertion_independence: The left side is the code's output and the right side is the path composition the code owns; the test-supplied value is only the inherited PATH, so the assertion does not compare a value against itself. Its scheduler element is computed by reckon.nested_launch.shim_directory, the function dispatch_launch.py:651-655 delegates to, so a defective relocation of that directory would be mirrored on both sides; the independent part is the /usr/bin tail and the git-shim exclusion.
evidence_limits: No suite rerun and no test rerun; the reviewed run's recorded arms were read instead.
The gate log header does not print its partition; the all_debug submission is read from the worker's verify-gate invocation recorded in stream.jsonl, and the log header prints a grid host.

The successful gate ran from a submission with RECKON_WORKER_FENCE unset, which the manifest and evidence fragment both disclose after three fenced submissions refused at a bind before pytest started.

The gate log the manifest records (scoped-gate-1795073282606964777.log) is at the reviewed head; the fragment quotes an earlier successful gate at f509cb35b0 (scoped-gate-1795072499630076643.log); both read 7 passed EXIT=0.

findings.text: non-blocking: the expected scheduler entry is computed by calling the product's own shim_directory() rather than an independent literal, so a defective relocation of the shim directory is mirrored on both sides; the assertion still guards the path-composition rule the repair is about, but not the shim path's value.
